# DeckArt

Purpose: reusable assets for manufacturers' business presentations. Transparent PNG illustrations, opaque PNG backgrounds, and SVG icons, diagrams, charts and explanation parts. Japanese usage descriptions and Japanese/English search terms; stable English IDs. Assets and metadata: CC0-1.0. Code: MIT.

Entry to share: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sakurai-yoshi/deckart/main/llms.txt
Repository: https://github.com/sakurai-yoshi/deckart
Pinned raw base for this edition: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sakurai-yoshi/deckart/v2.0.0/

## Select, retrieve and compose

1. Identify what the slide needs to communicate. Browse catalog.txt under the pinned raw base: it lists every asset ID and title, grouped by kind. Consider illustrations, backgrounds, icons, diagrams, charts and explanation parts as appropriate to that purpose. Kind, format and recolor filters are optional choices, not defaults.
2. Use catalog.json to compare candidates by use_case, message and keywords. These describe examples and pictured meaning, not an allowed-use list. An asset can support other contexts that fit its appearance. Select assets for their contribution to the slide; there is no required quantity or category mix.
3. Open preview_path for candidates. If preview_has_example_labels=true, the preview includes example text to show how the diagram, chart or part communicates; that text is for selection. Read metadata_path for the depicted relationships and available editing features. Choose from the image and the slide's content together. Illustrations' composition describes framing, facing and people count; it does not specify position or size.
4. Download path, the original asset rather than the selection preview, from the SAME pinned raw base and save the response bytes with the declared format extension. Verify sha256. PNG files live under media/; SVG files under assets/. The supplied file can be inserted directly. RAG bulk metadata is catalog.ndjson, one asset per line. Generation definitions under sources/ are historical production records; their prompts do not set conditions on using the artwork.
5. Compose around the actual text, data and visual hierarchy. Keep the image's proportions when scaling. Backgrounds can fill the slide, occupy part of it, or be cropped; a white panel or other overlay can improve text contrast. Position and size are decided in the presentation. View the rendered slide and adjust text fit, contrast, unintended overlaps, clipping and the meaning conveyed by the combination.

width/height describe pixels for PNG and viewBox units for SVG; canvas describes the asset's own coordinate system. These fields do not prescribe slide layout. transparent=true indicates PNG alpha; false indicates opaque PNG; null means SVG transparency is not classified. preview_path is a lightweight PNG preview, an SVG with example labels, or the original SVG where labels are unnecessary. preview_has_example_labels identifies labeled examples. A labeled preview does not mean those words are embedded in path: SVG source files may contain geometry without explanatory text. Use path for the final image and add the slide's actual text.

CC0 permits editing, cropping and recoloring in your own software. The export tool's supported operations below describe its capabilities, not restrictions on using the artwork.

## Local search and export

Python 3.10+ and a repository checkout or unpacked release ZIP are sufficient. No package, account or API key is needed.

Search by purpose in Japanese or English. Related candidates are ranked; filters are optional. The default page has 20 results. Use next_offset for the next page, or --limit 0 for all matches. Review alternatives across kinds when the subject supports more than one visual treatment.

    python3 scripts/library.py search '品質改善の流れを説明する'
    python3 scripts/library.py search 'quality improvement' --offset 20
    python3 scripts/library.py search '' --limit 0
    python3 scripts/library.py show illustration/explaining
    python3 scripts/library.py export illustration/explaining --output ./exports/explaining.png
    python3 scripts/library.py export background/cover-prismatic-depth --output ./exports/cover.png
    python3 scripts/library.py export icon/person --accent '#005BAC' --output ./exports/person.svg
    python3 scripts/library.py export process/approval-return --example-labels --output ./exports/approval-preview.svg
    python3 scripts/library.py export --request examples/progress-data.json --output ./exports/progress.svg

Search returns UTF-8 JSON with total, returned, next_offset, filters and assets. Show returns detailed metadata. Export writes an image plus a JSON sidecar and returns file, format, mime_type, metadata, sha256 and render. The sidecar records source ID, version, raw_base, path and hash; generation.definition_path and preview_path resolve against source.raw_base. --stdout emits image bytes. Existing output files require --force. Errors return JSON on stderr and exit code 2.

## Export capabilities

request.schema.json defines id, optional format (matching the source), accent, monochrome, labels, include_example_labels and data. metadata.render describes each asset's supported operations.

- PNG: copies the original file and alpha. Recoloring, drawing text into the image, data rendering and format conversion are outside this tool. False monochrome/include_example_labels and empty labels leave the image unchanged. Add text separately in the presentation or edit the image with your own software.
- SVG theme: default blue, arbitrary #RRGGBB accent or monochrome. Semantic signal colors remain distinct. Pale brand colors are adjusted for contrast; resolved colors and adjustments are returned. See themes.json.
- SVG labels: an optional way to include text inside the exported SVG. metadata.labels lists label-N IDs, internal boxes, font sizes and text limits. Supply labels such as {"label-1":"申請","label-2":"確認"}. The tool reports text that exceeds those boxes. Write the slide's actual text freely in PowerPoint, or use labels when it fits the supplied geometry. With a data request, include_example_labels=true adds the labels computed from that data. SVG text uses the listed system-font fallbacks; geometry-only export has no font dependency.
- SVG charts: distributed values are sample data. metadata.data_input describes supported inputs. Export recalculates geometry and numeric labels together; supplied values are marked is_sample=false.

Use one tag or commit consistently for lookup, metadata and original image bytes. A modified export records both its output hash and its source so the final file remains traceable.
